knowledge_point.title: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Products

question.:question/problem:
Simplify the expression, using the sine of twice the given angle.

$$
\left(\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)+\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)^2
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Put $x=\frac{\pi}{6}$. Expand the square and combine the squared terms.

$$
\begin{aligned}
(\sin x+\cos x)^2 &=\sin^2 x+2\sin x\cos x+\cos^2 x \\ &=1+2\sin x\cos x \\ &=1+\sin(2x)
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $\sin^2 x+\cos^2 x=1$ and $2\sin x\cos x=\sin(2x)$. The cross-term sign is positive.

Substitute $x=\frac{\pi}{6}$ and double the whole angle: $2x=\frac{\pi}{3}$. The result is

$$
1+\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) .
$$

knowledge_point.title: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Products

question.:question/problem:
Simplify to a constant multiple of a single trigonometric ratio.

$$
\frac{-3\cos\left(71^\circ\right)\sin\left(71^\circ\right)}{\cos\left(142^\circ\right)}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Put $x=71^\circ$. Recall $2\sin x\cos x=\sin(2x)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{-3\sin x\cos x}{\cos(2x)} &=-\frac{3}{2}\frac{2\sin x\cos x}{\cos(2x)} \\ &=-\frac{3}{2}\frac{\sin(2x)}{\cos(2x)} \\ &=-\frac{3}{2}\tan(2x)
\end{aligned}
$$

The denominator is nonzero, and $\tan(2x)=\sin(2x)/\cos(2x)$.

Substitute $x=71^\circ$ and double the whole angle: $2x=142^\circ$. The result is

$$
-\frac{3}{2}\tan\left(142^\circ\right) .
$$

question.:question/problem:
Simplify to a constant multiple of a single trigonometric ratio.

$$
\frac{-\frac{1}{2}\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{9}\right)\sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{9}\right)}{\cos\left(\frac{4\pi}{9}\right)}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Put $x=\frac{2\pi}{9}$. Recall $2\sin x\cos x=\sin(2x)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{-\frac{1}{2}\sin x\cos x}{\cos(2x)} &=-\frac{1}{4}\frac{2\sin x\cos x}{\cos(2x)} \\ &=-\frac{1}{4}\frac{\sin(2x)}{\cos(2x)} \\ &=-\frac{1}{4}\tan(2x)
\end{aligned}
$$

The denominator is nonzero, and $\tan(2x)=\sin(2x)/\cos(2x)$.

Substitute $x=\frac{2\pi}{9}$ and double the whole angle: $2x=\frac{4\pi}{9}$. The result is

$$
-\frac{1}{4}\tan\left(\frac{4\pi}{9}\right) .
$$
